title: A 1918 Cannon Fired a Shell 26 Miles Into the Sky

scenes.text: In 1918, a cannon fired a shell twenty-six miles into the sky.
That put it in the stratosphere, higher than any human-made object had gone before.
The Paris Gun, built by Germany, could hit targets more than eighty miles away.
Its shells left the barrel at over thirty-six hundred miles an hour.
They took about three minutes to reach Paris.
Twenty-six miles up, from a cannon.

description:
In 1918, Germany's Paris Gun fired shells up to about 26 miles high, into the stratosphere.
It could hit targets more than 80 miles away, with shells leaving the barrel at over 3,600 miles an hour.
Could you have built it?
first_comment: Bonus: it flew for about three minutes. Do you think a cannon could reach space?
